# Research Report

**Goal:** Explain the obligations that the EU AI Act imposes in 2026 on providers of general-purpose AI models, distinguishing obligations already applicable from later obligations, and identify authoritative Commission or EU sources supporting each conclusion. Prioritize EUR-Lex, European Commission, and EU AI Office publications.

## Questions
- (answered) Extract the entry-into-application rules and transitional deadlines from Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (specifically Articles 51-56 and 111) to establish the timeline distinguishing obligations active in 2025, 2026, and 2027.
- (answered) Identify core obligations for baseline GPAI and systemic-risk GPAI providers (transparency, copyright policy, summary of training data, model evaluations, cybersecurity) and retrieve recent European Commission and EU AI Office communications, draft/final Codes of Practice, and delegated acts.
- (answered) Synthesize findings to clearly distinguish obligations already in force prior to 2026, obligations newly or actively governing providers in 2026, and obligations deferred beyond 2026, referencing authoritative EU legal citations for every point.

## Synthesis
Under the EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689), general-purpose AI (GPAI) model providers in 2026 must adhere to the obligations established in Articles 51 through 56, which have already been applicable since 2 August 2025. Providers must maintain technical documentation, furnish documentation for downstream providers, publish a summary of training data, ensure compliance with EU copyright law, and fulfill specific systemic risk requirements if their models meet the systemic risk classification criteria.

Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 entered into force on 1 August 2024. Under the regulation's staged application schedule, GPAI model requirements operate on an earlier, distinct track compared to certain high-risk system timelines. Specifically, Articles 51–56 took effect on 2 August 2025, meaning that by 2026, obligations regarding technical documentation, downstream information sharing, training content summaries, copyright adherence, and systemic risk mitigation are fully active and enforceable against GPAI model providers.
